patch_description: Crossover of the two best-performing implementations. From the current program (score 0.54) I keep the exponentially-weighted robust local quadratic regression evaluated at the window end (zero phase lag, best accuracy: avg_error 0.28, correlation 0.94, noise reduction 0.57), but now I also retain the fitted local slope b for each window. From the Kalman/Holt inspiration program (lowest slope_changes 140.8 and false_reversals 114.6) I take the slope-gated reversal-suppression stage: a median filter on the estimated slope with a gate derived from local slope noise, followed by reintegration blended convexly (0.75/0.25) with the level-anchored regression output to prevent integrator drift. Finally, a light 3-tap smoothing pass plus a small slope-based forward extrapolation (lag_steps=1, using the quadratic fit's own slope, which is less noisy than the Kalman slope) compensates residual group delay without amplifying noise. This hybrid targets the weaknesses of each parent: the regression parent's relatively high slope_changes/false_reversals, and the Kalman parent's high lag/avg error.
